fatal_errors: The proposed titanium addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which is temperature-controlled nanoindentation and friction simulation of the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu/Cu system.
The stated 1 mm wear-depth limit is physically incompatible with an approximately 21 Å-thick coating and differs drastically from the target 30 Å indentation depth.
The proposed 600–900 °C range does not match the target 300–1200 K range or its critical transition near 900 K.
The oxide/cubic-phase mechanism does not address the target transition from stacking-fault/dislocation-mediated deformation to lattice disorder at high temperature.
The evidence comes from compositionally and structurally different bulk HEAs and does not establish titanium's effect in a FeNiCrCoCu coating on Cu.

The experiment does not specify atomically resolved measurements of HCP atoms, dislocation-line length, or lattice disorder, so it cannot adequately resolve the requested microscopic deformation mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad wear-resistance problem and supplies a clear modified-versus-unchanged comparison, so it is a conceivable alternative research direction. However, it does not recover the target intervention, thermal conditions, nanoscale geometry, mechanism, or temperature-dependent outcome. Its supporting literature only shows that titanium or protective oxides can improve wear in other HEA compositions and processing regimes; this is insufficient to justify transfer to the specified FeNiCrCoCu/Cu coating. The operating boundaries appear invented and include a wear depth many orders of magnitude larger than the coating thickness. Although the proposed wear-rate comparison is falsifiable at a macroscopic level, generic microstructure analysis would not discriminate the target atomistic deformation pathway.
